content: 1. Liposomal amphotericin B has been utilized as a treatment regimen for primary kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) in Bihar, India, as reported in Clinical Microbiology and Infection. 2. Burza S. and colleagues investigated combination therapies for visceral leishmaniasis in patients co-infected with HIV in India, with findings published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 3. Burza S., Mahajan R., Sinha P., van Griensven J., Pandey K., Lima MA, et al. evaluated the long-term effectiveness and treatment outcomes of liposomal amphotericin B (AmBisome) in visceral leishmaniasis and HIV co-infected patients in Bihar, India, as detailed in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases (2014). 4. A five-year field study by Burza S., Sinha PK, Mahajan R., Lima MA, Mitra G., Verma N., et al. demonstrated the long-term efficacy of a 20 mg/kg liposomal amphotericin B regimen for visceral leishmaniasis in Bihar, India, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases (2014). 5. Burza S., Sinha PK, Mahajan B., Lima MA, Mitra G., Verma N., et al. identified risk factors for relapse in immunocompetent patients treated with 20 mg/kg liposomal amphotericin B for visceral leishmaniasis in Bihar, India, as reported in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases (2014). 6. Casado JL, Lopez-Velez R, Pintado V, Quereda C, Antela A, Moreno S. documented cases of relapsing visceral leishmaniasis in HIV-infected patients undergoing successful protease inhibitor therapy, published in the European Journal of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (2001). 7. Casado JL, Abad-Fernández M, Moreno S, Pérez-Elías MJ, Moreno A, Bernardino JI, et al. highlighted visceral leishmaniasis as an independent cause of high immune activation, T-cell senescence, and lack of immune recovery in virologically suppressed HIV-1 co-infected patients, as detailed in HIV Medicine (2015). 8. Cascio A., Gradoni L., Scarlata F., Gramiccia M., Giordano S., Russo R., et al. conducted epidemiological surveillance of visceral leishmaniasis in Sicily, Italy, with findings published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine & Hygiene (1997). 9. Castro A., Ruiz-Giardin JM, Moreno J., San Martin JV, Carrillo E., Castro A. explored lymphoproliferative responses to soluble leishmania antigen (SLA) as a predictor of visceral leishmaniasis relapse in HIV-positive patients, published in Acta Tropica (2016). 10. Cenderello G., Pasa A., Dusi A., Dentone C., Izzo M., Toscanini F., et al. reported on the changing spectrum of clinical presentations in visceral leishmaniasis among HIV-positive patients, based on preliminary results from a clinical registry in Northern Italy, as published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society. 11. Cenderello G., Pasa A., Dusi A., Dentone C., Toscanini F., Bobbio N., et al. described the varied clinical presentations and mortality rates in a prospective registry of visceral leishmaniasis in a low-endemicity area of Northern Italy, published in BMC Infectious Diseases (2013). 12. Cipriano P., Miranda AC, Antunes I., Mansinho K. discussed the challenges of relapse and treatment failure in visceral leishmaniasis among HIV-infected patients, as detailed in Acta Medica Portuguesa (2017). 13. Colomba C., Saporito L., Vitale F., Reale S., Vitale G., Casuccio A., et al. identified cryptic Leishmania infantum infections in Italian HIV-infected patients, as reported in Parasites & Vectors. 14. Cota GF, de Sousa MR, de Assis TSM, Pinto BF, Rabello A. investigated circulating Leishmania DNA as a prognostic marker in chronic relapsing visceral leishmaniasis among HIV-infected patients, published in Acta Tropica (2017). 15. Cota GF, de Sousa MR, de Mendonça AL, Patrocínio A., Assunção LS, de Faria SR, et al. examined the clinical presentation and outcomes of leishmania-HIV co-infection in an urban area in Brazil, as detailed in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases (2014). 16. Coutinho JVSC, Santos FSD, Ribeiro RDSP, Oliveira IBB, Dantas VB, Santos ABFS, et al. conducted a comparative study on visceral leishmaniasis and leishmaniasis-HIV co-infection, published in the Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical (2017). 17. Daher EF, Fonseca PP, Gerhard ES, Leitão TM, Silva Júnior GB. described the clinical and epidemiological features of visceral leishmaniasis and HIV co-infection in 15 patients from Brazil, as reported in the Journal of Parasitology (2009). 18. Davidson RN. documented cases of visceral leishmaniasis relapse in patients co-infected with HIV and treated with liposomal amphotericin B, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases (1994). 19. Davidson RN, Di Martino L., Gradoni L., Giacchino R., Russo R., Gaeta GB, et al. conducted a multi-center trial on the use of liposomal amphotericin B (AmBisome) for Mediterranean visceral leishmaniasis, as detailed in the Quarterly Journal of Medicine (1994). 20. Del Giudice P., Mary-Krause M., Pradier C., Grabar S., Dellamonica P., Marty P., et al. evaluated the impact of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) on the incidence of visceral leishmaniasis in a French cohort of HIV-infected patients, published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases (2002).
